overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body for the city's public school district, responsible for policy, budgeting, and the appointment of the superintendent. Between November 2024 and October 2026, the committee managed a leadership transition from an interim to a permanent superintendent while advancing major infrastructure projects. Much of the committee's work involves coordinating with the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) for a comprehensive high school renovation and addressing district-wide facilities needs. As of the most recent meeting, the committee is developing a new strategic plan and refining elementary enrollment policies.

threads.name: Medford Comprehensive High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a multi-year project to renovate or replace the high school, starting with the appointment of building committee members and reaching an enrollment agreement with the MSBA for 1,395 students. The project advanced through the selection of Left Field as the Owner's Project Manager and the subsequent approval of a formal educational plan. Recent work has addressed a 999-year property deed restriction and the establishment of sustainability goals, such as LEED Silver certification. The committee continues to refine the space summary and design to maximize efficiency before finalizing schematic designs.

threads.name: Superintendent Leadership and Selection
threads.summary: Following the departure of Superintendent Edouard-Vincent in early 2025, the committee appointed Dr. Suzanne Galusi as interim superintendent to ensure continuity during budget and facility projects. After a period of transition and a formal performance evaluation, the committee voted in early 2026 to appoint Dr. Galusi as the permanent superintendent rather than conducting an external search. A final three-year contract was approved in May 2026. The committee subsequently realigned the superintendent's evaluation schedule to match the academic year.

threads.name: HVAC and Capital Infrastructure Upgrades
threads.summary: The committee approved significant capital projects to address failing HVAC systems and obsolete refrigerants at multiple schools, starting with a $25.7 million bond for the McGlynn and Andrews schools. Efforts then shifted to the Roberts Elementary School, where the committee reviewed a facilities assessment identifying over $83 million in needed repairs across the district. In mid-2026, the committee approved a $22.7 million schematic design for HVAC electrification and roof replacement at the Roberts school. Ongoing maintenance now includes the installation of district-wide security cameras and vape detectors.

threads.name: After-School Program Expansion
threads.summary: To address extensive waitlists, the committee partnered with the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) for a consultancy to reform its programs. This led to a restructuring that increased capacity by 150 seats, introduced full-time site directors, and established a new tuition rate card to fund specialized curriculum leaders. By late 2026, the administration reported a 68% reduction in the after-school waitlist. The committee continues to monitor capacity and has appointed new leadership for the programs.

threads.name: Elementary School Overcrowding and Grade Reconfiguration
threads.summary: Persistent overcrowding, particularly at Roberts Elementary, prompted the committee to move preschool classes and explore district-wide restructuring. While a proposal to change the district to a K-4, 5-6, and 7-8 grade span was discussed, the committee voted in July 2026 to delay any middle school grade configuration changes until at least 2028. Recent efforts have focused on drafting an intra-district elementary enrollment policy to manage reassignment requests. A formal task force was also established to review facility utilization and strategic space planning.

threads.name: Vocational (CTE) Program Admissions
threads.summary: High demand for vocational programs led the committee to adopt a new Chapter 74 admissions policy that utilizes a non-weighted lottery system for oversubscribed majors. The committee also approved the expansion of vocational offerings, including a new plumbing program. To enhance student opportunities, an honors pilot was introduced in late 2026, allowing juniors and seniors to earn honors credit through co-ops or capstone projects. The committee also maintains a viability form for the MSBA that tracks current enrollment and waitlist data.

threads.name: Generative AI and Technology Policy
threads.summary: In response to emerging technology, the committee developed and approved a comprehensive policy on the use of generative artificial intelligence in schools. The policy addresses ethical use, bias checking, and environmental impacts, and was incorporated into district student handbooks. In 2026, an additional amendment was passed prohibiting educators from using AI tools to grade qualitative student work. The committee also approved a five-year contract to modernize district printing and secure print management.

periods.narrative: This period was defined by the transition from Superintendent Edouard-Vincent to interim leadership and the authorization of millions in bonds for urgent HVAC replacements.
During this term, the committee appointed Dr. Galusi as permanent superintendent and advanced the high school building project into schematic design and educational visioning.
